title: API, SDK, resources and spans
summary: What OpenTelemetry is made of, what a span holds (kind, attributes, events, status, links), and how .NET's own Activity is the tracing API.

steps.title: API, SDK, exporter, Collector
body: OpenTelemetry (OTel) is a vendor-neutral standard and a set of libraries for traces, metrics and logs. Four parts:
- **API**: what code calls to create telemetry. It does nothing on its own (a no-op), so libraries can depend on it safely. In .NET
the API is built into the runtime: `System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource` / `Activity` for traces, `System.Diagnostics.Metrics.Meter`
for metrics, and `ILogger` for logs. ASP.NET Core, HttpClient, Npgsql and EF Core already call it.
- **SDK**: what the *application* adds to make it real (the `OpenTelemetry` NuGet packages): providers that listen, samplers, processors,
and the **resource** that says who is sending.
- **Exporter**: sends the data, usually as **OTLP** (the OpenTelemetry protocol, gRPC on 4317 or HTTP/protobuf on 4318).
- **Collector**: a separate process that receives, processes and forwards telemetry to backends (module 4).
A **resource** describes the entity producing telemetry and is attached to everything it sends: `service.name` (required in practice:
without it you get `unknown_service`), `service.version`, `service.instance.id`, `deployment.environment.name`, plus host, container and
Kubernetes attributes from detectors.
```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
.ConfigureResource(r => r.AddService("shop", serviceVersion: "1.4.2"))
.WithTracing(t => t.AddSource("Shop.App").AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation().AddOtlpExporter());

steps.prompt: You maintain a NuGet library used by many teams. How should it emit traces?
options: Create an `ActivitySource` and start activities; let each application decide whether to add the OpenTelemetry SDK and an exporter
Reference the OpenTelemetry SDK and configure an OTLP exporter in the library's static constructor
Reference a vendor's agent so traces always arrive
steps.explain: Libraries use the API only (in .NET: System.Diagnostics, no extra package). With no listener `StartActivity` returns null and costs almost nothing. The application owns the SDK, the sampler, the exporter and where data goes.

steps.title: Anatomy of a span
body: A **span** is one timed operation. In .NET it is an `Activity`. It has:
- a **name**: low cardinality, the *kind* of work (`GET /api/products/{id:int}`, `checkout`), never ids or raw URLs;
- **trace id** (shared by the whole request), **span id**, and **parent span id** (which makes the tree);
- a **kind**: `Server` (handles an incoming request), `Client` (makes an outgoing call), `Internal`, `Producer` / `Consumer` (messages);
- start time and duration;
- **attributes**: typed key/values (`http.route`, `db.query.text`, `app.cart.size = 3`);
- **events**: timestamped points inside the span (an exception, "cache miss");
- **status**: `Unset` (the default: fine), `Ok` (explicitly fine; rarely set) or `Error` with a description;
- **links**: pointers to spans in *other* traces (a batch job that processes 50 messages links to each message's trace).
This is a real product-page request from the lab: the shop calls inventory, then runs one query. Look at the bar lengths: almost all of
the 93 ms is one database span. Open it to read `db.query.text`.

attrs.db.query.text: SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE product_id = $1
attrs.db.system.name: postgresql

attrs.db.query.text: SELECT rating, body FROM reviews WHERE product_id = $1 ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 5
attrs.db.system.name: postgresql

steps.prompt: Match each operation to its span kind.
pairs: A SQL query sent by Npgsql
A worker handling a message from a queue
Computing the price of a cart in memory
steps.explain: Kind tells the backend how to draw service maps: a Client span in one service and the Server span it caused in another are an edge between the two. A database is a Client span with no matching Server span (the database does not trace itself).

steps.prompt: Per the HTTP semantic conventions, which spans get status **Error**? (select all that apply)
options: A client span whose call got a 409
A client span whose call timed out (no response)
steps.explain: Servers mark only 5xx as errors (a 4xx is the caller's mistake, not the server failing); clients mark 4xx and 5xx, and any failure to get a response. You can see both in the lab's failed checkout: inventory's server span for the 409 is Unset, the shop's client span for it is Error. Set `error.type` too (the status code, or the exception type).

steps.prompt: No SDK, no listener. What does this print?
steps.explain: With nobody listening to `Shop.App`, `StartActivity` returns null: no allocation, no cost. That is why instrumentation always uses `?.`. The same happens when the SDK listens but the sampler drops the trace, or when you forgot `AddSource("Shop.App")`: a classic "my spans never show up" bug.

steps.prompt: Complete the span: an attribute, an event, and an error status.

steps.title: Instrument a checkout with Activity
prompt: Write `void Checkout(ActivitySource source, string payment, int items, bool declined)` that records, with the .NET tracing API:
2. inside it, a child span `reserve stock` of kind `Client`;
3. when `declined`: an event `card.declined` on `checkout` and status `Error` with the description `card declined`.
The tests listen with an `ActivityListener` (what the SDK does for you) and read the spans back. Always use `?.`: when nobody
starter: void Checkout(ActivitySource source, string payment, int items, bool declined)
solution: void Checkout(ActivitySource source, string payment, int items, bool declined)
hints: `using var activity = source.StartActivity("checkout", ActivityKind.Internal);` ends the span when the method returns.
The child: `using (source.StartActivity("reserve stock", ActivityKind.Client)) { }` started while `checkout` is `Activity.Current`, so it becomes its child.
template: using var dojoListener = new ActivityListener { ShouldListenTo = s => s.Name == "Dojo.Shop",
Dojo.Check("a checkout span", dojoCheckout is not null, "spans: " + string.Join(", ", dojoDone.Select(a => a.DisplayName)));
Dojo.Check("app.cart.size is an int 3", dojoCheckout?.GetTagItem("app.cart.size") is int dojoSize && dojoSize == 3, "got " + dojoCheckout?.GetTagItem("app.cart.size")?.GetType().Name);
Dojo.Check("reserve stock is a Client child of checkout", dojoChild?.ParentSpanId == dojoCheckout?.SpanId && dojoChild?.Kind == ActivityKind.Client, "");
Dojo.Eq("a good checkout keeps status Unset", "Unset", dojoCheckout?.Status.ToString());
Dojo.Check("declined: a card.declined event", dojoBad?.Events.Any(e => e.Name == "card.declined") == true, "");
Dojo.Check("no listener: no crash, no spans", dojoDone.Count == 0, "");

steps.title: Draw the waterfall
prompt: A backend receives spans as a flat list and draws the tree. Do it yourself. Spans are
`record SpanRec(string Id, string? Parent, string Service, string Name, double Start, double Dur, string Status);` (milliseconds).
Write `List<string> Waterfall(List<SpanRec> spans)`: depth-first from the root (the span whose parent is null or not in the list),
children in order of `Start`, one line per span, indented two spaces per level:
**Self time** is the span's duration minus the sum of its direct children's durations (never below 0). Durations with `F1`.
Append ` ERROR` to the line of a span whose `Status` is `"error"`.
solution: var kids = spans.Where(c => c.Parent == s.Id).OrderBy(c => c.Start).ToList();
var self = Math.Max(0, s.Dur - kids.Sum(k => k.Dur));
foreach (var k in kids) Walk(k, depth + 1);
foreach (var root in spans.Where(s => s.Parent is null || !ids.Contains(s.Parent)).OrderBy(s => s.Start)) Walk(root, 0);
hints: A recursive local function `Walk(span, depth)` that adds its line, then walks `spans.Where(c => c.Parent == s.Id).OrderBy(c => c.Start)`.
Roots: `Parent is null || !ids.Contains(Parent)` (a parent that was never exported still leaves a root).
